text: Gambians tend to favor an indirect style of communication. It would be rare to find somebody who would directly ask for something without spending some time getting to the point. For example, if someone needs money, they will explain the situation and then tell you they are about to sell their only goat when what they really want is for you to volunteer the amount they need. When it comes to joking, Gambians tend to be direct. For example, if somebody is jokingly asking you for something, they will directly say “Give me your bicycle”, but if they are really in need of something, they will be indirect. Gambians are non-confrontational for the most part. Confronting someone directly will only deeply offend that person and make the problem even worse. Instead, Gambians find a third party, an intermediary, to help solve the problem. Gambians usually react with colorful sighs and gasps in reaction to happy or sad news. They repeat words or phrases a lot. Most all conversations begin with greetings. One asks about the family, the work, or a recent event. Then they go and talk about the weather, usually how brutally hot it is. During greetings no one goes into the truth about a certain difficulty one is having; that comes later in the conversation.

A little less than an arm’s length of personal space is acceptable during conversations. This space tends to be greater between members of the opposite sex and less for friends and family. It is common to see men hold ing hands with other men while walking and talking. This is a sign of friendship T ouching while talking is accepted for men with men and women with women , but between genders there is usually no touching and more personal space given . Men and women, husband and wives are rarely seen in public sitting next to each other, touching each other, or walking closely side by side. Intimacy is usually shown between members of the same sex. In offices or in the city, women and men’s interaction are a bit more relaxed. When speaking to peers of the same sex , direct eye contact is acceptable W hen speaking to elders or people of authority, indirect eye contact is the most appropriate. In the rural areas, women, girls, and boys do not make direct eye contact with male elders. White women have honorary male status, so elder men may offer their hand to shake while greeting.

The runs on “In Shallah” time, or “god willing.” No one is truly expected to be on time. Public transport runs on its own schedule, so if you get a taxi after only fifteen to thirty minutes of waiting, you are in the right place at the right time. Social programs usually start two to four hours after their posted time. School children are routinely thirty minutes to an hour late to school. State business runs on approximate time, the higher ranking the visitor the later they are entitled to be. Business meetings at private organizations run on a “tighter” schedule than public institutions, perhaps an hour or less later than the posted time, depending on setbacks from travel or weather. Professionals tend to be more punctual in business situations. Often times Gambians joke that GMT stands for Gambia Maybe Time, or WAIT stands for West African International Time. The roles of women in are slowly changing. Women are expected to be wives and mothers, but more and more women are also having careers. Girls’ education is a high priority of the current president, so most girls are now enrolled in school. However, is still very much a male-dominated society. In rural areas, women rarely drive, ride a bicycle, or go to groundnut fields. Women do not tell men what to do or defy a man’s instruction. Nonetheless, women’s social circles are vibrant and empowering to an extent. They have vegetable garden cooperatives and grassroots micro credit schemes. Men and women don’t typically socialize outside of their family. Unacceptable behavior for women would involve smoking, drinking, visiting non-relative males alone. Foreign women should dress conservatively and avoid very revealing or tight-fitting clothing. It's best to avoid short shorts or skimpy skirts as a woman's thighs are to a Gambian man what the breast is to most westerners. Foreign women are often seen as honorary men. They can eat and socialize with men, unlike Gambian women in rural areas. They can go to a mosque, but not go inside it. Gambian women will often give foreign women a hard time for not knowing how to cook, wash clothes by hand, or fetch water. But, this is part of the intense joking culture that persists here. Women must dress conservatively when outside the resort areas. Gambian women never show from their belly button to below their knees. Foreign women should do the same. Do not wear shorts or short tops, it is very, very rude and culturally insensitive.

Circling the index fingers around in front of the chest indicates that you will return or do something later. Hissing , ie. saying "psssst" , is common when trying to get someone’s attention, like a passerby or even a waiters in a restaurant. Burping after a meal is accepted as a positive sign that the food was good and enjoyed by the guest/customer . Clasp two hands together when acknowledging someone’s presence from afar. Pointing with the index finger is traditionally rude. Many people use their thumb or whole hand. When calling someone to come, people bend their fingers in toward themselves in a scratching motion. Always use your right hand to shake, eat or accept gifts. The left hand is used for cleaning oneself after using the ‘bathroom.’

Looking elders directly in the eyes and not greeting people properly are also rude. It is a serious insult to call somebody rude or accuse someone of stealing. The thumbs up sign is a rude gesture. If hitchhiking, people wave an arm at cars to stop. Asking too many personal questions can be seen as rude. Do not take pictures of any military personnel, they will most likely severely intimidate you and confiscate your camera.

The legal drinking age is 18 and not heavily enforced. The is ninety-five percent Muslim and Islam prohibits alcohol consumption. As you move farther away from the coast it is almost exclusively Muslim. There are some ethnically Christian groups that harvest and sell palm wine and cashew liquor. There are numerous restaurants, bars, and clubs in the city and on the coast that tourists and Gambians frequent. The majority of men smoke all over the country. Islam does not allow women to smoke. Foreigners can smoke at the resorts and restaurants in the city, but should not smoke in public when venturing outside the city. Penalties for possession, use, or trafficking in illegal drugs in are severe, and convicted offenders can expect long jail sentences and heavy f ines.

Visitors should dress nicely and modestly. Most Gambians do not expect tourists to know the greetings in the local language, but definitely appreciate it when foreigners do know some greetings in Wollof, Mandinka, or Pula Women must dress conservatively when outside the resort areas. Gambian women never show from their belly button to below their knees. Foreign women should do the same. Do not wear shorts or short tops, it is very, very rude and culturally insensitive. Sex tourism is a thriving industry here, whereby older European women come for relations with much younger Gambian men. The consequence of this is a lot of harassment of foreign women. There is the general expectation that white women are here only for sex or marriage. A ll over the country, but especially in popular tourist areas, bumsters , or young Gambian men whose job it is to make friends with foreigners, will harass you and try any means to get you to talk to them. Usually ignoring them is the best way to get rid of them. Sometimes sternly telling them to ‘go away, your not interested,’ works. Dress conservatively as a means to show that you are here to see the country and not here for sex. Overall, as a single female traveler expect harassment.

For Men - Slacks with a buttoned down dress shirt. For businesses in the city most men wear suit and tie. For Women - For conducting business anywhere in the country, including the city, most women wear a komplet. This is a traditional outfit with some western influence that includes a top with short or long sleeves, an ankle length skirt, and a head tie. Komplets are colorful, intricately designed, sometimes with fancy and flashy fabric. Women also wear slacks with a blouse. In the city, many women wear a pant or skirt suit. Skirts and dresses should always be to the knees .
Mr., Ms. and Madam are the most common titles used when meeting people in a business setting. When giving and receiving business cards, it is always advisable to do so with the right hand.

Meetings with local government officials and/or NGO employees begin when everyone gets there. If you show up on time, expect to wait an hour. It's proper to g reet the entire room first. Then greet the highest ranking male or male elder and from there go around the room. As a woman, remember to verbally greet men, unless the man offers his hand. Small talk is expected; in fact it is part of the greeting. Go around and ask everyone about their morning, family, health, and work. Two to five minutes will suffice. Before the meeting begins the highest ranking male or male elder leads the group in an Islamic prayer. There also can be no one leading the prayer, whereby everyone attending prays silently. After prayer, the leader of the meeting welcomes all those attending in order of importance. Meetings here can last up to eight hours. Every one has something to say about everything. Usually it is mostly men at the meetings, so therefore they feel entitled and expected to offer their opinions about all matters on the agenda. Once the meeting is finished, it is closed with another Islamic prayer.

Bargaining is a big part of the culture. In the markets, similar to flea markets in North America , you can find everything from fabric to vegetables, artwork to shoes, clothing to jewelry. In the city the markets are huge, while up country they vary in size. Gambians tend to hike up the prices when they see a foreigner. Most speak the local languages, but some speak English in and around the city. Bargaining is expected. Start really low and act like you really don’t care if you buy the item or not. Show emotion. If the vendor will not bring the price down to where you want it, then start to walk away. At this gesture the vendor will accept your last price. Sometimes the vendor won’t budge and let you walk away. At this point you have to decide if you really want the item. Bartering can take anywhere from two to ten minutes. Food prices are usually set. In the local small shops, called bitiks, all prices are set. In any indoor shop away from the market area, albeit clothing or food, all prices are set. One exception is the fabric and clothing indoor stores that are located on the fringes of an open air market.

The school year at most universities begins in September and ends in July. University students dress nicely and are generally well-groomed. They often wear western-style clothes, but will also wear African styles as well. V ery revealing or tight-fitting clothing, such as short shorts or skimpy skirts would be unacceptable for women. The grading system at most universities is on 1-9 scale, with 1 being the highest. The pass/fail line is usually a 7 or 8. Lecture is the most common form of teaching.

Drinking is acceptable for students within the Christian community, but is 90% Muslim so many places won't serve alcohol or allow it to be brought in. Being drunk in public is not accepted and could get you into trouble. Smoking is acceptable but it is very uncommon among female students and women in general. As far as dating goes, Gambians don’t really go out on dates. They tend to hang out in their compounds with friends, so if 2 people are dating one of them will go to the other's place to visit. Usually they go with a friend, not alone. This is more the case is rural areas vs. urban ones. Dating is done mostly by the youth. In the rural areas, from the age of fifteen and up, girls are expected to get married. In the city, women are single and date up into their twenties. Gambian men to be very forward. A man may tell a woman he’s just met that he loves her. Women usually play hard to get at first, so as not get a reputation. In many areas, t he men are supposed to court the women for two to three weeks, declaring their love and sending overly sappy and poetic love texts. This verbose and flowering love vernacular is used always when expressing feelings about the opposite sex. Greetings are extremely important. To get anything done, you should greet people first. You can’t just walk into a room without greeting everyone, at least in a general way.

애 국적 재정향 및 건설 동맹 (Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Construction, APRC) - 국민화해당은 아다마 바로우가 대통령 후보였던 2016년 연립의 일부였고 그 후 하마트 바가 관광문화부 장관으로 재직하면서 국민화해당은 바로우 정부의 핵심 설립 연도: 1996년 구성원이 되어 왔음 당수: 파바카리 자타(Fabakary Jatta) 정치적 입장: 우익 2017년 이래 이 당은 바로우 대통령이 주도하는 연립 정부의 일부가 되어 이데올로기: 반(反)식민주의, 종교적 보수주의, 우익 대중주의 왔음 APRC는 1994년의 쿠데타를 계획했던 육군 장교들이 설립하였으며 자메 대통령 치하에서 1996년부터 2016년까지 여당이었음 라.

감비아의 날(Gambia Day)은 중국에서 열린 <2019년 베이징 중국 국가 주석 시진핑(習近平, X Jnpng)과 회동함 원예박람회(Beijing Horticultural Expo 20>에서도 기념되었음 í ì í 2018. 2월 기준, 감비아 국민 중 절대다수(96.4%)가 이슬람교이며, 11세기 중반에 이슬람교가 전파된 것으로 알려져 있음 샌디사원(Sandy Mosque) 사회 문화 1.

문화 자료: My Magazine 기 독교는 국민 중 3.5%이며, 이슬람교 휴일과 기독교 휴일이 모두 공휴 일임 감 비아의 이슬람교는 샤머니즘(Shamanism)과 수피즘(Sufism)의 영향을 많이 받았음 종 교적 측면에서 볼 때 감비아는 관용적이고 세속적 경향이 강함 - 다만, 야히아 자메 대통령 집권 시기에는 한때 13개월 동안 감비아의 국명이 ‘감비아 이슬람 공화국’으로 바뀐 적도 있었으나 자메가 퇴임한 후에는 감비아 공화국으로 되돌려짐 Gambia 82 Republic of Ghana 감비아공화국 개황 83 Ⅶ 사회 문화 2. 신문사 of The Gambia)이고, 다른 하나는 미국 국제대학 서아프리카 캠퍼스 (American International University West Africa)임 감 비아에는 총 11개의 신문이 있는데, 이들은 인쇄본과 온라인을 통해 정치, 경제, 사회, 문화, 스포츠 등 다양한 주제를 다루고 있음 1 999.

팹 사이네(Pap Saine), 데이다 하이다라(Deyda Hydara), 바부카르 가이 (Babucarr Gaye)가 설립했으며 정치적 입장은 중도 성향을 보임 84 Republic of The Gambia 감비아공화국 개황 85 Ⅶ 사회 문화 ② 주요 격주 신문: Foroyaa 4. 문화 세 레쿤다(Serrekunda)에 본사를 두고 있는 영자 신문 Foroyaa는 1987. 관습과 전통 7월에 설립됨 감 비아의 8개 종족 집단은 다양한 방식으로 혼례와 장례를 치르는데 이 신문사의 소유주는 ‘독립과 사회주의를 위한 인민 민주 조직(PDOIS) 특히 이슬람교도는 이러한 의례를 과도하게 치르는 경향이 있음 당’임 기 독교도는 출생, 사망, 혼인과 관련된 관습에서 지역적으로 다른 양상 을 보이고 있음 나.

문학 여성 중 76%, 13세 이하 소녀 중 51% 이상이 할례를 경험했다는 결과가 있는데, 가부장제 전통의 일부인 여성 할례는 건강과 교육적 측면에서의 감비아 문학은 구전 문학과 문자 문학으로 구성되며 구전 문학은 전통적 문제뿐만 아니라 사회적 편견에 따른 많은 문제를 유발함 그리오(griot, 졸라어로 gewel)와 다양한 형태의 의례 시를 포함하는데, 문화 전승의 지배적 유형임 나. 예술 및 공예 - 파이의 아랍 시 중 하나는 “Mimaah Kathalil Baitil Lassa”인데, 이 시는 독립 기념일 ① 직물 퍼레이드에서 감비아 경찰 악단이 자주 부르는 노래임 감 비아의 홀치기 염색한 천과 납결 염색한 천(batik)은 화려하고 색조가 또 한 감비아의 다양한 이슬람 학자는 아랍어, 월로프어, 풀라어, 만딩 다양하며 이들 천은 모든 관광 시장에서 볼 수 있음 카어로 이슬람교 신학에 관한 저서를 출판함 감비아 여성의 전통 의복 라.
